forms.label: ている past polite
forms.negative: チンしていませんでした

definitions.gloss: to microwave; to heat up in the microwave
definitions.explanation: Casual, colloquial verb meaning to heat food in a microwave oven. Named after the 'chin' (ding) sound that microwaves make when finished.

examples.japanese: ⟦お{弁当|べんとう}→お弁当：02864_obentou⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧チンして。
⟦{冷|つめ}たく→冷たい：00681_tsumetai⟧⟦なったら→なる：01970_naru⟧、チンすれば⟦いい→いい：00118_ii⟧⟦よ→よ：09475_yo⟧。
examples.english: If it gets cold, just pop it in the microwave.

examples.japanese: ⟦{昨日|きのう}→昨日：00859_kinou⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{残|のこ}り{物|もの}→残り物：18299_nokorimono⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧チンして、⟦{夕飯|ゆうはん}→夕飯：02981_yuuhan⟧にした。
examples.english: I microwaved yesterday's leftovers and had them for dinner.

notes:
An onomatopoeic ⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧-verb derived from the チン sound (ding) that Japanese microwaves make when finished heating. Extremely common in casual speech — most Japanese people use チンする rather than the formal ⟦{電子|でんし}レンジ→電子レンジ：04973_denshirenji⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{温|あたた}める→温める：02096_atatameru⟧.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- チンして⟦{食|た}べる→食べる：00396_taberu⟧: to microwave and eat
- チンする⟦だけ→〜だけ：03093_dake⟧: just microwave it (describing easy meals)
- ⟦レンジ→レンジ：01047_renji⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧チンする: to ding it in the microwave

USAGE:
Used in casual, everyday conversation. Not appropriate in formal writing. The word is understood by virtually all Japanese speakers regardless of age. Convenience store staff may ask: ⟦{温|あたた}めます→温める：02096_atatameru⟧⟦か→か：09473_ka⟧？ (Shall I heat it up?) — the formal equivalent of チンする.

RELATED WORDS:
- ⟦{電子|でんし}レンジ→電子レンジ：04973_denshirenji⟧: microwave oven (the formal word for the appliance)
- ⟦{温|あたた}める→温める：02096_atatameru⟧: to heat up, to warm (the formal verb)
